meta.title: Retirement Simulator — Monte Carlo Retirement Planning
meta.description: Stress-test your retirement plan against thousands of simulated market futures. Free, private, and it runs entirely in your browser.

hero.badge: Monte Carlo engine · runs in your browser
hero.subtitle: The engine replays your whole financial life through thousands of simulated markets — volatility, inflation, pension, and spending — so you see the full range of outcomes before you bet your retirement on a single guess.
hero.note: No sign-up. No cloud. Your data never leaves this browser.
hero.lede: One average return tells you nothing.

features.title: Everything a serious plan needs
features.subtitle: A complete planning engine — no spreadsheet gymnastics required.

monteCarlo.title: A real Monte Carlo engine
monteCarlo.body: Lognormal returns sampled with the Box–Muller transform — thousands of complete market lifetimes, computed in seconds.

live.title: Instant what-if answers
live.body: Move any slider and the percentiles redraw in about 100 milliseconds. Interrogate every assumption, live.

phases.title: Both halves of the journey
phases.body: Accumulation to drawdown in one model: savings growth, statutory pension, one-time windfalls, and custom expense streams.

reports.title: Reports worth sharing
reports.body: Export a clean, comprehensive PDF of your plan — assumptions, charts, and recommendations included.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.body: No account and no tracking of your finances. Parameters persist only in your browser's local storage.

bilingual.title: Bilingual & localized
bilingual.body: Full English and German interfaces with proper currency, number, and date formatting throughout.

how.title: From guess to plan in five minutes

step1.title: Describe your plan
step1.body: Ages, assets, savings, pension, and spending — a guided setup that takes about five minutes.

step2.title: Run thousands of futures
step2.body: The engine replays your entire financial life through simulated markets — good decades and bad.

step3.title: Stress-test and refine
step3.body: Tune assumptions live, watch the bands respond, and export the PDF once the plan holds.

cta.title: Know where you stand.
cta.subtitle: Five minutes of setup. A lifetime of clarity.

footer.tagline: Monte Carlo retirement planning — free, open, private.
footer.copyright: © {year} Retirement Simulator. Runs entirely on your device.

spread.body: These are the assets left at age {endAge} in the sample plan above. Nothing changed but the order in which the market delivered its returns — and that alone decides whether the plan ends comfortable or uncomfortably thin.

median.label: Median run
median.body: The middle outcome — the single number a spreadsheet would have shown you on its own.

high.label: Best 10% of runs
high.body: A kind market. Ten times the ending balance of the unlucky case, from the same inputs.

legalRetirementAge.tooltip: Official retirement age when pension benefits begin. In Germany this is typically 67 years old.

endAge.label: Planning Until Age
endAge.tooltip: Age until which to run the simulation. Typically life expectancy (85) plus buffer. Longer planning periods require more conservative withdrawals.

currentAssets.label: Current Assets (€)
currentAssets.tooltip: Total value of your current investments, savings, and retirement accounts. This is your starting point for wealth accumulation.

annualSavings.label: Annual Savings (€)
annualSavings.tooltip: How much you can save and invest each year until retirement. Higher savings rates lead to earlier retirement possibilities.

annualSavingsGrowthRate.label: Savings Growth Rate
annualSavingsGrowthRate.tooltip: Expected yearly increase in your annual savings before retirement, reflecting income growth.

monthlyPension.label: Monthly Pension (€)
monthlyPension.tooltip: Expected monthly pension from the government system, starting at legal retirement age. This reduces your required private savings.

oneTimeIncomes.label: One-time incomes
oneTimeIncomes.tooltip: Add lump-sum inflows such as insurance payouts, home sales, or inheritances. These are invested at the start of the year following the age you choose.

capitalGainsTax.label: Capital Gains Tax
capitalGainsTax.tooltip: Tax rate on investment gains when selling to cover expenses. German rate: 26.375%. This affects your net withdrawal rates.

averageROI.label: Average ROI
averageROI.tooltip: Expected annual return on investments. Historical stock market: ~7-10%. Bond portfolio: ~3-5%. Diversified portfolio: ~6-8%.

roiVolatility.label: ROI Volatility
roiVolatility.tooltip: Standard deviation of returns. Higher volatility means more uncertainty. Conservative: 5-10%, Moderate: 10-15%, Aggressive: 15-25%.

averageInflation.label: Average Inflation
averageInflation.tooltip: Expected annual inflation rate. ECB target: 2%. Historical average in developed countries: 2-3%.

inflationVolatility.label: Inflation Volatility
inflationVolatility.tooltip: How much inflation varies year-to-year. Historical range: 0.5-1.5%. Higher volatility creates more uncertainty in retirement costs.

simulationRuns.label: Number of Runs
simulationRuns.tooltip: Monte Carlo simulations to run. More runs = higher accuracy but slower computation. 1000+ recommended for reliable results.

withdrawalStrategy.label: Withdrawal Strategy

note.dynamic: Rows show every retirement year using Vanguard Dynamic Spending: first-year expenses start from the plan, then target spending is {withdrawalRate} of the prior year-end portfolio and is bounded by {ceiling} / {floor} guardrails versus inflation-adjusted prior spending. monteCarlo.title: Monte Carlo simulation
monteCarlo.description: This report employs Monte Carlo simulation, a computational technique that uses repeated random sampling to model the probability of different outcomes in retirement planning.

timeSteps.implementation: Annual projections with monthly granularity for expenses

variables.vt: V(t) = Portfolio value at time t

percentiles.title: Percentile calculations
percentiles.description: The report presents three key percentiles from the simulation results:

p10.title: P10 (10th percentile)
p10.detail: Pessimistic scenario – 90% of outcomes exceed this value

p50.title: P50 (50th percentile / median)
p50.detail: Central tendency – half of outcomes above, half below

p90.title: P90 (90th percentile)
p90.detail: Optimistic scenario – only 10% of outcomes exceed this value

success.title: Success rate definition
success.description: A simulation run is considered successful if the portfolio maintains a positive balance through the entire planning horizon (age {age}). The success rate represents the percentage of all simulation runs that meet this criterion.

items.distribution: Returns are assumed to follow a normal distribution, which may not capture extreme market events
items.inflationModel: Inflation is modeled as constant in real terms across all expense categories
items.taxPolicy: Tax rates and regulations are assumed to remain constant
items.unexpected: No consideration for unexpected one-time expenses or windfalls
items.healthcare: Healthcare costs may increase faster than general inflation
items.pension: Pension benefits assumed to be inflation-adjusted and guaranteed
